review:
Playing this game was a mistake—because after finishing it, I feel like I’ve witnessed the absolute peak of gaming greatness, and nothing else will ever come close to this again. Especially while playing the Blood and Wine DLC, it felt overwhelmingly emotional.
That subtle smile from Geralt at the very end—when he finishes talking to Regis and looks directly into the camera at you—leaves behind an emptiness best described as "Post-Witcher Depression." After spending well over a hundred hours meticulously crafting Grandmaster Griffin gear, completing every single contract and side quest, and living in a breathing world like Toussaint, it feels less like finishing a video game and more like coming to the end of a long personal journey.
Blood and Wine isn't just an expansion; it is CD Projekt Red's royal farewell letter to Geralt and the players. After the dark, war-torn atmosphere of the base game and Hearts of Stone, stepping into the sunlit vineyards of Toussaint, experiencing the emotion of the fairytale realm, witnessing the sacrifice of a true friend like Regis, and finally finding a permanent home at Corvo Bianco is enough to make anyone emotional. In the history of fantasy RPGs, it is truly hard to find anything that matches the narrative depth and the soulful bond The Witcher 3 builds with its characters.

# The Witcher 3 Review

## 1. Atmosphere & Level Design — 10/10

**World — 10/10:**  
With the remaster and what my rig can offer, I feel like I'm getting the best of everything this game has to offer visually. This remaster is exactly how I remember this game aging in my head. It is just as beautiful to play today as it was when it first came out. Every zone feels unique, and every location feels like it has a reason to exist.

**Level Design — 10/10:**  
From swamps to cities, islands and Vikings, to France-inspired regions and wine country, every environment builds upon the world with masterful storytelling. Every area feels worth exploring and taking the time to appreciate.

**Exploration — 10/10:**  
This game is a completionist's dream. So much to do, so much to discover, and so much to explore.

## 2. Characters & Companions — 9.33/10

**Main Character — 10/10:**  
Geralt is one of my favorite fictional characters. Even though we're constantly told he has no emotions, I think he displays more meaningful emotion than most characters. He's witty, sarcastic, and ultimately tries to be a force for good in a world filled with cruelty and horror.

**Companions — 10/10:**  
There is so much lore behind every companion and character you meet. Honestly, the romance options are fantastic too. It's always difficult to choose, and that's a good problem to have.

**Character Development — 8/10:**  
Probably the weakest point of the category. It's not necessarily that these characters evolve or develop dramatically. Many are already established, and I think there's something special about seeing them remain true to who they are. The score is an 8 because your choices can still lead to some pretty bad outcomes. That's part of what makes it an RPG.

## 3. Story — 9.67/10*

**Main Story — 10/10:**  
I love the hunt for Ciri. Having read the books, played the other games, and watched the shows, the story feels incredibly compelling.

**Writing — 10/10:**  
Even the DLCs are masterpieces in writing. So much of the storytelling is built around relationships, right and wrong, and the moral grounds you're willing or unwilling to stand on.

**Pacing — 9/10:**  
The story has great pacing. As a completionist, though, F the Skellige island markers scattered across the ocean and getting stuck in the swamps. Haha. The story keeps you engaged, and there's always something to keep a completionist busy.

**Ending:**  
The main ending is great. Hearts of Stone is amazing, and Blood and Wine is perhaps the best DLC ever made.

## 4. Combat & Gameplay — 9.75/10

**Combat — 10/10:**  
This is my favorite RPG combat system in any game. The modern controls and quick casting refresh were amazing. You can do so much without it feeling like a hassle, and the new finishers are fantastic.

**Gameplay Loop — 10/10:**  
I'm a completionist. There's plenty to do. Enough said.

**Progression — 9/10:**  
Leveling feels fair, even starting fresh on Death March. My only complaint is that I found it nearly impossible to acquire all the ability points needed for the additional mutagens and slots, even after completing the main game and both DLCs. I also wasn't able to craft every Grandmaster gear set, only the two I was testing builds with.

**Variety — 10/10:**  
I never really felt bored playing this game, with the exception of those Skellige question marks out in the ocean.

# Final Score

Atmosphere & Level Design: 10/10  
Characters & Companions: 9.33/10  
Story: 9.67/10*  
Combat & Gameplay: 9.75/10

**Overall: 9.69/10**

**Final Thoughts:**

This is probably not even a top five game for me, but it's definitely top three. Even then, it might actually take the top spot as my favorite video game of all time. Hundreds of hours across PS4, Xbox, and now Steam. I've finally gotten around to reviewing it.

Easy contender for best rpg ever made without question. The combat feels amazing and looks beautiful. The gear progression feels well paced and offers a wonderful selection of weaponry and armor. The missions are incredibly written, causing you to be enthralled in even the most basic of errands. The enemies are fascinating, and cause me to regularly find myself reading through the beastiary just for funsies. The maps are awesome, with plenty to check out and plenty to do. And, as I am sure anybody with internet access knows by now, the game is absolutely GORGEOUS.

Gwent though? Oh my god is gwent so rigged. It's like walking into a casino that doesn't even bother pretending like you could win lol. 

Imagine this, You spend 30 minutes going all across the map purchasing gwent cards from anyone who has some to sell. After a while you decide to use your new paper arsenal against the populace in order to take their cards too. You think about who the easiest opponent to start with would be, and eventually settle on a villager in the middle of a swamp who lives almost entirely alone. you think to yourself "what cards could this swamp man possibly have?" and prepare for an easy battle. In the first match he surprises you with a decent amount of frontline and ranged cards, but not enough to overwhelm you, and you win the round. With the first round finished, all you need to do is to place every unit card you have and overwhelm him in the the second round for the win, so you do so. in response the man places a single melee card, with a total of 6 points to offer. You may not realize in this moment, but you have already lost. Before you can think, the old man places a card that kills your highest point card. you replace it with a soldier card, its worth 1 point... Immediately after the old man drops ANOTHER death card, and kills 2 ranged cards who boosted each other up to 10 points, you lose 20... Now you have 11 points total. like a small hare struggling in the mouth of a fox as it is dragged away, you play your final unit card. like the 3 cards you still have in play, it's a ranged card. It doesn't boost anybody, or give you an extra card, just gives the 4 points, but as far as you know right now? That's enough. So you play it, and pray to whichever god you believe in. How does your god answer your prayers? The old man plays a weather card, all 4 of your ranged cards are now worth 1 point each. You have 4 points, he has 6. You have no more unit cards. He has 1 card you don't know. You think "Wait! there's no way that last card of his is a unit card, not this late in the round, it has to be a weather card or special card! this could still be a win if I use my weather card!" So you do and play your final card, now his only unit card in play is worth 1 point. "4 against 1, and there's no way you have another unit card to play, I HAVE this." you think to yourself, another false hope. The old man plays a ranged unit card, but he plays it to your side. 5 against 1 now... which would almost be a comfort, if you didn't know what comes after that is. As fast as a blink, the old man draws 2 cards from his deck... You don't manage to catch a glimpse of either one, yet you still feel the dread. With no cards to play and no other choice, you pass, and leave your fate in the old mans hands. Before you can get out a second prayer, the old man plays a siege unit card, which lays in the only part of the battlefield that remains unaffected by weather cards. It's worth 8 points. 5 against 9, it's over, it's a bust... but it isn't over, not until HE says it is. The old man plays a second siege card, it's worth 1 point, but it has a boost to other siege units. He has 12 points to your 5. You lose, and it's all your fault for your ignorance. Little did you know that this swamp man with 32 syllables in his name is actually a legend of old. He is a comic con yu-gi-oh! tournament master who retired to play gwent against the drowners in the swamps of velen. And you are just one of many victims to suffer underestimating his card fueled warpath.

Played The Witcher 3 more times than I can count. All the way back in 2015 on PC(GOG) and I’ve also completed it on PS4. When I heard about the remaster and the new DLC coming out in 2027, I knew I had to go back one more time.

Having 100% completed it, I can now safely say this is easily one of the greatest games of all time. No one tells a story quite like CDPR and everyone should experience the Bloody Baron questline at least once in their life. There is truly nothing else like it.

That said, the remaster isn't without it's issues. Visual bugs pop up, environments(especially indoors) can be excessively dark and performance takes a hit with ray tracing or path tracing enabled. In Novigrad, the framerate drops to nearly half of what it is elsewhere in the game. Going for all the achievements was also a headache, particularly with Gwent cards tied to NPC's that occasionally become unresponsive. These bugs have been around since day one and have never been fixed.

Still, these are minor complaints for a game that remains pure joy.
The Witcher 3 is a fun game with a rich storyline, but its visuals and the flexibility of character controls are lacking.

游戏内容真不错，推荐给那些真正喜欢冒险剧情的玩家。次世代整整玩了3遍所有内容，重制版通关本体后才真正的感觉腻了。剧情没得说，玩了几次都很好玩，就像看电影一样怎么都看不腻。中文配音也是味真足，你觉得捧读并非是因为配音演员技术不行，而是蠢驴自己审核要求的字正腔圆，只有几处小支线的情绪表达有点儿素材复用的感觉。
战斗系统确实很不错，天赋流派设计很出色，但就是一周目很难吃饱，导致你必须开控制台或者二周目去继续体验。但二周目的数值乱填导致你非常脆皮，不玩瘾头吃煎药根本扛不住BOSS和某些小怪的普通一击，属于好机制遇到了烂数值，某种程度上还原了原著但却没完整还原。就算如此，打完二周目你也不会腻，毕竟一周目玩腻了刀剑，谁不想体验二周目的大法师杰洛特？零帧起手法印轮读毁天灭地，叶和特看到了也得说一句NB。强到你会觉得敌人太弱了，然后开启死而无憾难度，再被路边野狗一口咬死，最后老老实实的降低难度。这就是蠢驴的神秘数值设计，就像隔壁2077你不拉高难度就会觉得设定崩坏一样。所以游玩的时候不要把某种打法优化的太猛，只要自己玩的舒服就行。数值的终点是瘾头，机制的终点是法印，狄拉夫会让你见识到艾瑞汀有多丢人，二周目再教你真实的杰洛特有多脆皮。
重制版算是我的四周目了，先通了本体，剩下的放到明年等旧时曲一起玩。

review:
就冲波兰蠢驴的次世代，重制+新dlc上，必须给一个好评。
从剧情和任务设计上，巫师三无疑是十分优秀的，无论是游戏中的次要角色，还是主要角色，都被塑造的栩栩如生，个性鲜明。巫师三的魅力永远都源自选择，从故事的最开始我们就要做出选择，这些选择不仅仅只是影响当下，有些时候我们做出的选择，会在后续的游戏一直影响着我们。游戏偏中世纪的风格与法术的结合，给出了一种完全不同的中世纪体验。
但巫师三作为一款已发售十余年之久的游戏，自然存在一些问题，战斗系统稍繁冗且单一，总结起来就是叠buff+法印+砍砍砍。巫师道具是这个题材的一大特色，但是作为一款需要上百小时通关的游戏，会不会有点太单一了呢，虽然技能树以在一定程度上改变法印的效果，但是仍旧显得平平无常。近几年广受好评的游戏，就拿cyberpunk2077举例，游戏里无数的枪支类型与流派搭配，可以让玩家花费很大的经历去研究，但这一点显然是巫师三最大的诟病。
overall，作为一款2015年发售的游戏，波兰蠢驴对这一ip的重视我们都有目共睹，剧情的叙述，角色的构造和任务的设计都是十分出色的，但游戏的战斗玩法在如今百花齐放的2026年显得过于单一。

CDPR对巫师3的重置再次做到了教业界所有忘了初心但不忘赚钱的制作组和发行商做人，你们的游戏卖的不好跟什么都没有关系，老子的游戏连盗版都不用防照样卖爆！

本人是重制版重新入坑的，游戏已经在steam里躺了很多年，初见时由于比较稀松（真实…）的操作手感、开局可怜的背包和负重、以及初期缓慢的成长节奏劝退，后来有多次想要重新入坑，但都担心自己已经没有从前的那种耐心品味这样一个慢节奏的传统RPG

还好制作组听劝，在重制版中选择性舍弃了所有所谓的真实，但从最初就是为了延长玩家游戏时长的设计，也再次证明了一款真正的好游戏是不需要这些设计的，当制作组有信心抛弃他们时艺术才真正大成

而我想说同时波兰蠢驴也是聪明的，如果没有这样的重置和免费推送，如同我这样的玩家应该是永远也不会尝试去完成游戏，最多就是继续躺在我steam的收藏夹里，而如今的我肯定不会错过明年的旧时曲

应该感谢制作组用这次重置让如我一般如今已经没有多少耐心和时间的人能够再次被一款游戏的叙事所打动，找回了不知多少年前那种吃好糠的感觉，在如今每天都有新游，每月都有大作的时代，却已经很久没有一款游戏让我觉得值得会议，或者当我做完一个任务却只奖励给我1点经验点的时候不会觉得”我C，浪费了我这么多时间“，而是回味不止。甚至会感觉在巫师3中徜徉一小时，完成几个任务，比看一个小时的猎魔人美剧更有故事感。一个RPG做到如此程度确实可以做游戏业的教科书

再说点儿实际的，我在无攻略的情况下达成了猎魔人结局，没想到养娃的心得在游戏中起了作用，对于本作的战斗手感，很遗憾即便是重制版也没有改善太多，这里推荐安装这个“菠菜冷面・BCAQ战斗增强MOD”，可以自定义战斗手感和顿帧，装上后个人感觉战斗乐趣大大提升，只是没想到把RPG元素做到这么炉火纯青的CDPR竟然在这上面还是就差这么点儿火候


我们很难知道巫师3启发了多少作品，也有很多游戏制作声称受到了巫师的启发，但真正愿意花力气去学的至少从结果上来看寥寥无几，但正因为有这样的游戏和制作组在，才让人看到了游戏业的未来

最后，巫师3仍然不是完美的，我在过程中还是遇到了一些会导致任务无法继续或人物卡住的BUG，让我想到了这几天看到的一些外媒对影之刃零的评价，如巫师3一般缝缝补补了11年的神作尚且如此，对一个新作吹毛求疵不免目光狭隘，无非是因为我们的3A和制作公司还远非主流，我们的文化输出还不够，赶在影之刃零的前一天打完了巫师3的重置，希望以后我国的厂商和作品也能继续给这个行业带来感动和惊喜！
